Gatwick Airport Shuttle Transit

The Gatwick Airport Shuttle Transit is a 3⁄4-mile (1.2 km) long elevated automated people mover that links the North and South Terminals at London's Gatwick Airport. The line is ground-side, and besides linking the two terminals also serves to link the North terminal to the airport railway station. Although sometimes colloquially, but erroneously, known as a "monorail", the transit vehicles are carried on rubber tyres running on a concrete track with twin running surfaces and are steered by separate guide rails.

Until 1987, Gatwick had a single main terminal, now known as the South Terminal. The first people mover was opened on 26 April 1983, running a short distance between the main South Terminal and a small circular satellite pier containing additional departure gates. This was the UK's first automated people-mover system. This system has since been replaced by a walkway-and-moving walkway link, although the remains of the elevated guideway are still visible; in the years since, they have been partially demolished to provide additional headroom to the airside service road below. In 1987, the new North Terminal was opened. A longer-distance people mover was constructed to connect the new terminal to the existing South Terminal and the adjacent railway station, still in service today. The line initially used Adtranz C-100 people-mover cars, which remained in operation until September 2009, by which time they had travelled a total of 2.5 million miles (4 million km). Gatwick began upgrading its shuttle service in April 2008, with a bus replacement service in place from September 2009. A new operating system and shuttle cars (six Bombardier CX-100 vehicles) was installed, and the guideway and transit stations were refurbished at a total cost of £45 million. The system re-opened on 1 July 2010, two months ahead of schedule; it featured live journey information and sensory technology to count the number of passengers at stations.

The transit has two parallel guideway tracks, running on a concrete elevated structure with an emergency walk-way between the tracks. There are enclosed stations at each terminal, which allow boarding from a central platform between the tracks while passengers disembark to platforms outside the tracks. Doors on the edges of each platform line up with the train's doors. There is no connection between the two tracks, each of which hosts a single three-car train shuttling backwards and forward. The line is automatic and driverless. The normal service uses both trains, with a departure from each terminal every 5 minutes and a 2 to 3 minute journey time. The service operates 24-hours a day, although service levels are reduced to every 10 minutes between 23:00 and 06:00, with only one of the two guideway tracks being used. No fares are charged.

To: All Design and Production Staff 
From: Creative Development Office 
Date: October 8, 2026 
Subject: Guidelines for Development, Documentation, and Distribution of Knitting Patterns

The purpose of this memorandum is to establish a consistent framework for the creation and management of knitting patterns across all product lines. All new patterns must be drafted using the standardized template that includes a clear title, gauge information, yarn recommendations, and a concise description of the intended garment or accessory. The template should be completed in the designated software, and a PDF version must be generated for internal review before any external release. This process ensures that each pattern meets our quality criteria and can be easily referenced by both staff and customers.

When drafting a pattern, designers are required to verify that all measurements are based on a 4-4-4 gauge using the specified yarn weight. Any deviation from this standard must be noted in the pattern notes, and a corresponding swatch should be attached to the documentation. All stitch abbreviations must follow the glossary established in the 2024 Pattern Reference Manual, and any new abbreviations must be approved by the editorial team before inclusion. Consistency in terminology reduces confusion and supports a smoother workflow from design through production.

Intellectual property considerations remain a priority. All patterns developed in-house are the exclusive property of the company and must be marked with the appropriate copyright notice on the first page of the PDF. If a pattern incorporates a motif or technique that is licensed from an external creator, the licensing agreement must be reviewed and the required attribution included verbatim. Unauthorized use of third-party designs will result in immediate disciplinary action and may expose the company to legal liability.

Distribution of patterns to retail partners and directly to consumers will follow the tiered release schedule outlined in the Marketing Calendar. Early-access releases are limited to a select group of flagship stores and must be accompanied by a feedback form that is returned within ten business days. Full public release will occur no earlier than thirty days after the final internal sign-off, and all promotional material must reference the official pattern code to facilitate tracking and inventory management. Any deviation from the schedule must be approved by the Director of Product Strategy.

Finally, all staff are reminded to maintain the confidentiality of unpublished patterns. Files should be stored on the secured server with access restricted to team members who have been granted explicit permission. When sharing drafts via email or collaboration platforms, ensure that the documents are password-protected and that the password is communicated through a separate channel. Adhering to these protocols protects the integrity of our creative assets and reinforces the professional standards that define our brand.

Please direct any questions regarding these guidelines to the Creative Development Office, and confirm receipt of this memorandum by responding to the attached acknowledgment form no later than October 12, 2026.

Fiona Lowry

Fiona Lowry (born 1974) is an Australian painter who airbrushes pale colours to portray landscapes with people in them. The landscapes are beautiful and ambiguous, provoking the dangerous side of wilderness. Lowry also paints portraits and won the 2014 Archibald Prize at the Art Gallery of New South Wales with a portrait of Penelope Seidler. She is represented in the National Gallery of Australia, as well as the state galleries of Australia and in private collections.

Lowry was born in Sydney (1974) and continues to work in Sydney. As a child she continually watched people and drew. Lowry had a religious upbringing, and has told interviewers that she see the beauty and the foreboding in nature. This is reflected in her artworks. Lowry completed a Bachelor of Visual Arts, Honours, at the Sydney College of the Arts.

Since 2001, Lowry has airbrushed her canvases in pale, monochromatic colours that create a sense of ambiguity with the harshness of some of her subjects. Often set in bushland/forest where historically bad events have occurred including massacres of Aboriginal people and murders, Lowry's work have a sense of danger or vulnerability. In 2010 she had her first solo exhibition in Sydney. She was represented by Gallery Barry Keldouli in Sydney until 2010. Today Lowry is represented by Martin Browne Contemporary, Sydney. Some of Lowry's landscapes include nude figures and in juxtapositions that are ambiguous-emotional or violent. These figures act out dramas in a modern wilderness setting. Her work's formal elements evoke beauty yet still harbour unease. Lowry has also incorporated portraiture into her work, again focusing on the psychological. Some of her figures in the landscape are portraits. In an interview Lowry noted that the Archibald Prize at the Art Gallery of New South Wales was her first experience of seeing art, and she wanted to be part of it. Lowry was a finalist in 2011 and 2013, and won the portraiture prize in 2016. with a portrait of Penelope Seidler. She had seen Seidler at an art exhibition and remarked on her beaury and presence. From that incident she wanted to paint her.

Lowry was awarded the Doug Moran National Portrait Prize in 2008. The $100,000 portrait prize for her painting What I Assume You Shall Assume, was a naked self-portrait set in the Belanglo State Forest a scene of menace as the site of the backpacker murders. She was the winner of the Fleurieu Art Prize in 2013 for her painting Alone With You. In 2013 the painting also won the Wynn Prize for landscape at the Art Gallery of New South Wales. The painting was completed during her residency at Arthur Boyd's estate at Bundanon that Boyd left to the nation. She was a finalist in the Archibald Prize in 2011, 2013, 2021 and 2022. She was the winner of the Archibald Prize in 2014 for her painting Penelope Seidler. In 2018, Fiona Lowry was awarded the $3000 Paddington Art Prize Honorable Mention for her work "My Mother's Far Embrace".

Fiona Lowry
Fiona Lowry (born 1974) is an Australian painter who airbrushes pale colours to portray landscapes with people in them. The landscapes are beautiful and ambiguous, provoking the dangerous side of wilderness. Lowry also paints portraits and won the 2014 Archibald Prize at the Art Gallery of New South Wales with a portrait of Penelope Seidler. She is represented in the National Gallery of Australia, as well as the state galleries of Australia and in private collections.
Lowry was born in Sydney (1974) and continues to work in Sydney. As a child she continually watched people and drew. Lowry had a religious upbringing, and has told interviewers that she see the beauty and the foreboding in nature. This is reflected in her artworks. Lowry completed a Bachelor of Visual Arts, Honours, at the Sydney College of the Arts.
Since 2001, Lowry has airbrushed her canvases in pale, monochromatic colours that create a sense of ambiguity with the harshness of some of her subjects. Often set in bushland/forest where historically bad events have occurred including massacres of Aboriginal people and murders, Lowry's work have a sense of danger or vulnerability. In 2010 she had her first solo exhibition in Sydney. She was represented by Gallery Barry Keldouli in Sydney until 2010. Today Lowry is represented by Martin Browne Contemporary, Sydney. Some of Lowry's landscapes include nude figures and in juxtapositions that are ambiguous-emotional or violent. These figures act out dramas in a modern wilderness setting. Her work's formal elements evoke beauty yet still harbour unease. Lowry has also incorporated portraiture into her work, again focusing on the psychological. Some of her figures in the landscape are portraits. In an interview Lowry noted that the Archibald Prize at the Art Gallery of New South Wales was her first experience of seeing art, and she wanted to be part of it. Lowry was a finalist in 2011 and 2013, and won the portraiture prize in 2016. with a portrait of Penelope Seidler. She had seen Seidler at an art exhibition and remarked on her beaury and presence. From that incident she wanted to paint her.
Lowry was awarded the Doug Moran National Portrait Prize in 2008. The $100,000 portrait prize for her painting What I Assume You Shall Assume, was a naked self-portrait set in the Belanglo State Forest a scene of menace as the site of the backpacker murders. She was the winner of the Fleurieu Art Prize in 2013 for her painting Alone With You. In 2013 the painting also won the Wynn Prize for landscape at the Art Gallery of New South Wales. The painting was completed during her residency at Arthur Boyd's estate at Bundanon that Boyd left to the nation. She was a finalist in the Archibald Prize in 2011, 2013, 2021 and 2022. She was the winner of the Archibald Prize in 2014 for her painting Penelope Seidler. In 2018, Fiona Lowry was awarded the $3000 Paddington Art Prize Honorable Mention for her work "My Mother's Far Embrace".

To: All staff members scheduled for the upcoming client engagement in Chicago 
From: Office of Travel Coordination 
Date: 8 October 2026 
Subject: Finalized travel itinerary and related instructions

The outbound flight for the Chicago delegation departs on Monday, 16 October, at 07:45 a.m. from Terminal 4 of the Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport. Passengers are assigned seats in the business class cabin; the airline has confirmed a direct service, with an estimated flight time of 2 hours and 15 minutes. Check-in opens three hours prior to departure, and the airline recommends arriving at the terminal no later than 04:45 a.m. to allow sufficient time for security screening and boarding. A reminder has been sent to all travelers to verify that their government-issued identification matches the name on the ticket and to ensure that any required visas or travel authorizations are current.

Upon arrival at Chicago O'Hare International Airport at approximately 10:00 a.m., a ground transportation team will be waiting at the baggage claim area. A white-label sedan will transport the group to the downtown Marriott Riverwalk hotel, where reservations have been made under the corporate account. Check-in time at the hotel begins at 3:00 p.m.; however, early check-in has been requested and will be granted on a first-come, first-served basis, subject to room availability. Each traveler will receive a room key card and a welcome packet containing Wi-Fi credentials, emergency contact numbers, and a brief guide to local dining options.

The business schedule for the three-day visit has been arranged to balance client meetings with internal debriefs. On Tuesday, the first full day, the team will convene at the hotel conference suite at 08:30 a.m. for a briefing led by the project manager, after which they will travel by chartered van to the client's headquarters for a series of presentations beginning at 10:00 a.m. Lunch will be provided on site, and the afternoon will include a facility tour followed by a working session. Wednesday's agenda mirrors Tuesday's structure, with an additional networking dinner at 07:00 p.m. at a nearby steakhouse, for which transportation has been pre-arranged.

Thursday marks the departure day. A continental breakfast will be served at the hotel, and participants are asked to pack personal items and settle any incidental charges by 11:00 a.m. The chartered van will collect the group from the hotel lobby at 12:30 p.m. and transport them to O'Hare for the return flight, scheduled to depart at 02:15 p.m. on United Airlines flight 512. Travelers should retain their boarding passes and travel documents until the trip is fully concluded.

Please review the attached travel confirmation PDFs for individual flight numbers, seat assignments, and hotel reservation details. Should any discrepancies arise, contact the travel office at extension 4421 no later than 5 p.m. on Friday, 13 October. Thank you for your cooperation and safe travels.

Schmidt number

In fluid dynamics, the Schmidt number (denoted Sc) of a fluid is a dimensionless number defined as the ratio of momentum diffusivity (kinematic viscosity) and mass diffusivity, and it is used to characterize fluid flows in which there are simultaneous momentum and mass diffusion convection processes. It was named after German engineer Ernst Heinrich Wilhelm Schmidt (1892-1975). The Schmidt number is the ratio of the shear component for diffusivity (viscosity divided by density) to the diffusivity for mass transfer D. It physically relates the relative thickness of the hydrodynamic layer and mass-transfer boundary layer. It is defined as:

S c = ν D = μ ρ D = viscous diffusion rate (molecular) mass diffusion rate = P e R e {\displaystyle \mathrm {Sc} ={\frac {\nu }{D}}={\frac {\mu }{\rho D}}={\frac {\mbox{viscous diffusion rate}}{\mbox{(molecular) mass diffusion rate}}}={\frac {\mathrm {Pe} }{\mathrm {Re} }}}

ν = μ ρ {\displaystyle \nu ={\tfrac {\mu }{\rho }}} is the kinematic viscosity (m2/s) D is the mass diffusivity (m2/s). μ is the dynamic viscosity of the fluid (Pa·s = N·s/m2 = kg/m·s) ρ is the density of the fluid (kg/m3) Pe is the Peclet Number Re is the Reynolds Number. The heat transfer analog of the Schmidt number is the Prandtl number (Pr). The ratio of thermal diffusivity to mass diffusivity is the Lewis number (Le).

K {\displaystyle K} is the mass diffusivity (m2/s). The turbulent Schmidt number describes the ratio between the rates of turbulent transport of momentum and the turbulent transport of mass (or any passive scalar). It is related to the turbulent Prandtl number, which is concerned with turbulent heat transfer rather than turbulent mass transfer. It is useful for solving the mass transfer problem of turbulent boundary layer flows. The simplest model for Sct is the Reynolds analogy, which yields a turbulent Schmidt number of 1. From experimental data and CFD simulations, Sct ranges from 0.2 to 6. Studies have shown that the turbulent Schmidt number varies locally within a flow, depending on both turbulence characteristics and flow parameters. Formulations have been derived to estimate it locally based on these quantities, providing a means to relate concentration and turbulence fields more directly.

For Stirling engines, the Schmidt number is related to the specific power. Gustav Schmidt of the German Polytechnic Institute of Prague published an analysis in 1871 for the now-famous closed-form solution for an idealized isothermal Stirling engine model.

The property management office has created this guide to help prospective tenants understand the standard procedures for securing a residential unit. Our goal is to make the leasing process as transparent and efficient as possible for all applicants. Please read these terms carefully before submitting any paperwork. Understanding these steps will help you avoid common delays that often occur during the initial application phase. It is important to note that all policies described here are subject to change in accordance with local housing regulations and company standards. By proceeding with an application, you acknowledge that you have reviewed and accepted these baseline requirements without reservation.

First, applicants must ensure they meet our standard financial and credit criteria to be considered. We require a gross monthly income of at least three times the rent amount for the desired unit. This determination is made by reviewing the last three months of pay stubs or a similar proof of income. Additionally, a hard credit check will be conducted upon receipt of the signed authorization form. Any adverse findings, such as late payments or evictions in the past seven years, may result in an automatic denial of the application. We reserve the right to request additional documentation if our initial review raises any questions regarding your financial stability.

Once your application is approved, you will be invited to schedule a time to review the lease agreement in person. The lease outline will include the rent amount, security deposit, and specific house rules that apply to your unit. You will need to sign and date the document, as well as return a copy of your government-issued identification. The security deposit is due in full on the day you sign the final lease. Please ensure that the check or digital transfer bears your printed name exactly as it appears on your identification documents. Failure to provide accurate details may cause a delay in accessing your new home.

After the move-in date, tenants are responsible for maintaining the property in a clean and livable condition. Damages beyond normal wear and tear will be charged to the tenant at the time of move-out. Normal wear includes minor scuffs on the walls or carpet, while damage includes broken windows or large holes in drywall. Our maintenance team is available twenty-four hours a day for urgent repairs, but routine requests should be submitted during business hours. You are also responsible for keeping contact information current with the front desk manager. This ensures that you receive important notices regarding building safety, utility changes, or scheduled maintenance.

Rent is due on the first day of each month and may be paid through our online portal, bank transfer, or check. A ten-percent late fee will be applied if the payment is not received by the fifth day of the month. Automatic withdrawal options are available and highly recommended to streamline this process. We encourage new residents to attend the welcome orientation session held on the first week of each month. This meeting provides a detailed tour of the facility and introduces you to your neighbors and staff. text:
The property management office has created this guide to help prospective tenants understand the standard procedures for securing a residential unit. Our goal is to make the leasing process as transparent and efficient as possible for all applicants. Please read these terms carefully before submitting any paperwork. Understanding these steps will help you avoid common delays that often occur during the initial application phase. It is important to note that all policies described here are subject to change in accordance with local housing regulations and company standards. By proceeding with an application, you acknowledge that you have reviewed and accepted these baseline requirements without reservation.

First, applicants must ensure they meet our standard financial and credit criteria to be considered. We require a gross monthly income of at least three times the rent amount for the desired unit. This determination is made by reviewing the last three months of pay stubs or a similar proof of income. Additionally, a hard credit check will be conducted upon receipt of the signed authorization form. Any adverse findings, such as late payments or evictions in the past seven years, may result in an automatic denial of the application. We reserve the right to request additional documentation if our initial review raises any questions regarding your financial stability.

Once your application is approved, you will be invited to schedule a time to review the lease agreement in person. The lease outline will include the rent amount, security deposit, and specific house rules that apply to your unit. You will need to sign and date the document, as well as return a copy of your government-issued identification. The security deposit is due in full on the day you sign the final lease. Please ensure that the check or digital transfer bears your printed name exactly as it appears on your identification documents. Failure to provide accurate details may cause a delay in accessing your new home.

After the move-in date, tenants are responsible for maintaining the property in a clean and livable condition. Damages beyond normal wear and tear will be charged to the tenant at the time of move-out. Normal wear includes minor scuffs on the walls or carpet, while damage includes broken windows or large holes in drywall. Our maintenance team is available twenty-four hours a day for urgent repairs, but routine requests should be submitted during business hours. You are also responsible for keeping contact information current with the front desk manager. This ensures that you receive important notices regarding building safety, utility changes, or scheduled maintenance.

Rent is due on the first day of each month and may be paid through our online portal, bank transfer, or check. A ten-percent late fee will be applied if the payment is not received by the fifth day of the month. Automatic withdrawal options are available and highly recommended to streamline this process. We encourage new residents to attend the welcome orientation session held on the first week of each month. This meeting provides a detailed tour of the facility and introduces you to your neighbors and staff. Your prompt attention to these responsibilities helps ensure a comfortable and safe environment for everyone living in the building. Thank you for choosing to live with us.

Subject: Final Agenda for Next Friday Team Offsite
Hi Team,
I am excited to share the finalized agenda for our upcoming team offsite next Friday. We have structured the day to balance collaborative strategy work with plenty of time for relaxation and informal networking. Please review the outline below so you can prepare any necessary materials or thoughts in advance of our departure.
The morning will begin with a brief welcome address at ninety minutes past eight. Following that, we will dedicate the next two hours to a deep dive into our quarterly goals and individual performance metrics. This session is crucial for aligning our departmental efforts, so please come with specific questions or concerns ready to discuss openly with the group.
Lunch is scheduled for twelve o'clock at the on-site dining hall. We plan to keep this meal informal to encourage casual conversation among cross-functional teams. After we resume at one thirty, we will break into smaller groups for creative brainstorming workshops focused on product innovation and customer experience improvements.
The final interactive session runs until four o'clock when we will reconvene for a summary of key takeaways. We will then head to the lounge area for a social mixer featuring light refreshments and an open question segment. This is a great opportunity to build stronger personal connections outside of typical work contexts.
Please confirm your attendance and any dietary restrictions by Thursday noon. Let me know if you have any logistical questions before then. I look forward to seeing everyone and having a productive and enjoyable day together as a unified team.
Best regards,
Sarah Jenkins
Director of Operations

China Construction America

Home | About | Contact

China Construction America (Chinese: 中建美国), founded in 1985, is a subsidiary of China State Construction Engineering Corporation Ltd. (CSCEC)-the world's largest construction and real estate conglomerate and the biggest global contractor-that operates on the East Coast of the U.S and the Gulf of Mexico, the Caribbean, and Latin America, having many finished and ongoing projects worldwide. CSCEC was ranked the 18th on Fortune Global 500 list. Headquartered in Jersey City, NJ, CCA operates mainly in New York, New Jersey, Washington, DC, South Carolina, North Carolina, Louisiana, Florida, California, the Caribbean, and Panama. CCA provides a range of construction services, such as program management, construction management, general contracting, design-build and public-private partnership assistance for public and private clients. CCA was ranked the 57th biggest contractors in the 2020 Engineering News-Record Top 400 Contractors list, the 35th biggest construction management-at-risk firms by ENR in 2020, the 35th on 2020 ENR Southeast Top Contractors, and the tenth on the Top Contractors in Bridges.

Founded in 1985, China Construction America (CCA) is a subsidiary of China State Construction Engineering Corp. Ltd. (CSCEC). In 2001, the CCA office in the World Trade Center was destroyed in the September 11 terrorist attacks, the company had to move its headquarters from the World Trade Center to Jersey City. On April 4, 2014, CCA acquired Plaza Construction, one of the nation's leading construction management and general contracting companies. The sale is prompted by the dynamic growth of Plaza and Fisher Brothers' desire to focus on the development side of their business. According to Richard Wood, the CEO of Plaza Construction, the acquisition is more about creating strategic relationships and sharing resources. During October 2014, the New York State Supreme Court judge ruled that contractor China Construction America (CCA) owed damages worth $1.6bn to the developer of the Baha Mar resort in the Bahamas, as CCA breached contracts and committed fraud to force the project out of the developer's hands.

cloud storage options

The landscape of digital life has fundamentally shifted toward the cloud, where files once confined to local hard drives now roam freely across the internet. This transition offers unparalleled convenience, allowing users to access their photos, documents, and media libraries from any device with an internet connection. However, with so many providers competing for attention, selecting the right storage solution requires a careful evaluation of needs, budget, and security considerations. Understanding the distinct features of major platforms can prevent frustration and ensure your data remains safe and accessible when you need it most.

Google Drive remains a top contender for those already embedded in the Google ecosystem. It integrates seamlessly with Docs, Sheets, and Slides, making it the ideal choice for teams and individuals who rely heavily on real-time collaboration. The service offers a generous free tier that includes 15GB of shared storage across all Google services. For power users, the paid plans expand this capacity significantly, though they come with a subscription fee that must be weighed against personal file requirements. Its strength lies in its integration, ensuring that your documents are always synchronized and editable from any location without manual uploads.

Apple iCloud appeals strongly to iPhone and Mac users who value privacy and seamless device synchronization. It handles backups, photos, and notes with a level of integration that few competitors can match. The ecosystem ensures that when you take a photo on your phone, it is instantly available on your tablet or computer. While the storage limits on the free plan are modest, the premium tiers provide generous capacity for those deeply invested in Apple hardware. This option is particularly beneficial for families using the shared iCloud+ plan, which allows multiple members to pool their storage needs easily.

Microsoft OneDrive stands out for enterprise environments and Windows users who depend on Microsoft Office. It provides robust business-grade security and administrative controls that personal accounts often lack. For everyday consumers, it maintains close ties to Office apps, ensuring that Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files are smartly managed and version controlled. The advantage here is the familiarity of the interface for anyone who has used the Microsoft suite for years, offering a steady and reliable experience without the steep learning curve sometimes associated with cloud platforms.

Finally, specialized services like Dropbox and Backblaze offer distinct advantages for specific needs. Dropbox excels in file sharing and team workflows, providing a clean interface and powerful sharing tools that surpass general-purpose drives. Backblaze, conversely, focuses on disaster recovery and simple, cost-effective backup solutions that sit quietly in the background. When choosing a provider, consider what matters most to you, whether it is collaborative power, ecosystem integration, or raw backup reliability. A hybrid approach using two different providers for different file types can often offer the best balance of security, accessibility, and value in an ever-changing digital world.

Cosmetic Valley

The Cosmetic Valley or pôle cosmétique sciences de la beauté et du bien-être (in English, cosmetic science of beauty and well-being business cluster) is a technopole, the most important French business cluster specialized in the production of consumer goods in the industry of perfumes and cosmetics in France.

The Cosmetic Valley stretches across three regions and seven departments: Centre-Val de Loire (Eure-et-Loir, Indre-et-Loire, Loiret and Loir-et-Cher), Île-de-France (Yvelines and Val-d'Oise) and Normandy (Eure). The headquarters of the cluster are located on the site of the Chartres Cathedral.

Eure-et-Loir has nearly 70% of companies in the sector. To department officials, the Cosmetic Valley is an essential element of the attractiveness of the territory, which would particularly illustrated by the introduction of foreign groups such as Reckitt Benckiser, but also small and medium enterprises (SMEs/SMBs) who joined the sector. Cosmetic Valley boasts the creation of over 1,500 jobs in the department in ten years.

University research : University of Orléans (Orléans-la-Source); Companies : Shiseido (Ormes), the center of R&D dedicated to perfumes and cosmetics of LVMH Recherche which includes Parfums Christian Dior, Givenchy, Guerlain and Fresh.

Cosmetic Valley has been founded in 1994 on the initiative of Jean-Paul Guerlain in the region of Chartres. This is the first industrial sector emerged in Eure-et-Loir. In 2005, the industries of Eure-et-Loir come together with those of the Loiret to be labeled "national competitiveness cluster" under the supervision of the government of Jean-Pierre Raffarin. The 25th of August 2006, a decree defines the area of research and development of the cluster. Municipalities of the department of Eure, Eure-et-Loir, Indre-et-Loire, Loiret and Yvelines are concerned. Rachel Georgia Wehl Lowe (German: [ʋeːl]; born 19 November 2000) is an Australian soccer player who plays as a forward or midfielder for Women's Super League 2 (WSL 2) club Durham and for the Australia national team. She previously played for Western Sydney Wanderers, Sydney FC, and Melbourne Victory, and played college soccer for UCLA Bruins.

Born in Sydney, Lowe grew up in the Inner West and Northern Sydney. She started her football career with West Pymble FC, playing in a mixed team alongside her twin brother, Edward, before joining Northern Tigers FC in 2011. After three seasons with Tigers, she joined the Football New South Wales Institute (FNSWI) program, where she was coached by notable coaches such as Leah Blayney and Craig Foster. She attended Pymbles Ladies' College. A natural sporting talent, Lowe also played girls cricket at State and National level, and for Gordon District Cricket Club.

Lowe committed to UCLA in 2018 and joined the Bruins in 2019. On 23 August 2019, she made her collegiate debut in a 3-0 victory against Iowa State, scoring her first goal in the 58th minute. Lowe chose not to return to the Bruins in 2020.

From 2016 to 2018, Lowe played for the Football New South Wales Institute (FNSWI) program in the NPL NSW, and scored 19 goals in 42 appearances for the side.

At age 15, Lowe signed with the Western Sydney Wanderers for the 2016-17 season and made her debut in Round 2 against Sydney FC. She made a total of 9 appearances for the club in her first season. In September 2017, she re-signed with the Wanderers. She finished the 2017-18 season with 1 goal in 8 appearances. In September 2018, Lowe re-signed for a third season with the club. She finished the 2018-19 season with 1 goal in 10 appearances. In June 2019, Lowe left Australia to join American college team UCLA Bruins.

Lowe was called up to represent Australia at the 2017 AFC U-19 Women's Championship, where she scored in a 5-2 victory against Vietnam, helping her side progress to the semi-finals. She made 5 appearances for Australia U20 at the 2018 AFF Women's Championship, scoring once against Timor-Leste. In February 2018, Lowe received her first call up to the senior team for the 2018 Algarve Cup in Portugal. She made her senior debut on 5 March 2018, coming on as a substitute in a 2-0 victory over China.

Gillian Clark (historian)

Edith Gillian Clark is a British historian, who is Professor Emerita of Ancient History at the University of Bristol. She retired from the University of Bristol in 2010. Clark is known for her work on the history, literature, and religion of late antiquity.

Clark studied Greek and Latin language and literature, ancient history, and philosophy at Somerville College, Oxford. She received her Master of Arts and Doctor of Philosophy degrees from the University of Oxford. She has taught at the universities of Glasgow, St Andrews, Manchester, Liverpool and Bristol. Clark is currently working on a commentary of Augustine of Hippo's City of God, under contract with Oxford University Press. She is a Fellow of the British Academy and an editor for the Translated Texts for Historians 300-800 series, published by Liverpool University Press. She is editor of the series Oxford Early Christian Studies and Oxford Early Christian Texts, published by Oxford University Press. An event, "Christianity and Roman Society: A Colloquium for Professor Gillian Clark", was held in her honour in 2011 at the University of Bristol and a Festschrift was published in 2014 as a result.

raw:
Bangalore Open Air

Bangalore Open Air (BOA) is India's only dedicated Heavy metal open air music festival which takes place yearly in Bangalore, India. The 11th edition of the festival in collaboration with Wacken Open Air took place in February 2024.

The Second Edition of the festival took place at Jayamahal Palace on 6 July 2013 and involved bands and artistes from eclectic genres of Heavy Metal. It was headlined by American metal band Iced Earth and Swedish melodic death metal band Dark Tranquillity. The event took place at Jayamahal Palace on 6 July 2013.

The Third Edition of the festival took place on 13 September 2014 and was headlined by Destruction and Rotting Christ. For the first time in the history of Heavy Metal Music the concept of crowd funding was adopted to fund a percentage of the festival. The 4th Edition of the Wacken Open Air Metal Battle, India presented by Bangalore Open Air was held from 19 April to 27 April. The prelims of the competition were held in Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Guwahati & Kolkata.

The 6th and most successful edition of G-Shock Bangalore Open Air was held on 1 July 2017 at Royal Orchid Resorts, Yelahanka, Bangalore( the third consecutive time at the same location.) The lineup consisted of bands from the sub genres of: death metal, thrash metal, and speed metal.

The 7th anniversary edition of G-Shock Bangalore Open Air was held on 7 July 2018 at Aadya Farms and Leisure Resorts, Yelahanka, Bangalore. This edition marked the maiden show of American thrash metal titans Overkill in India along with American death metal band Immolation and French post metal band Alcest, who brought their unique blackgaze sound to India after attempting do so since 2013.

The 8th edition of G-Shock Bangalore Open Air held on 9 February 2019 at Aadya Farms and Leisure Resorts, Yelahanka, Bangalore. Headlining acts include: Black metal giants Abbath and New York Technical death metal outfit Suffocation. On the day of the event the 4 winners of the regional editions of Wacken Metal Battle 2019 from the Indian subcontinent countries: Krur (Nepal), Mass Damnation (Sri Lanka), Trainwreck (Bangladesh), Nephele (India) compete to play for a coveted slot at the Wacken Open Air metal battle in Germany.

The 9th edition of Bangalore Open Air was scheduled for 21 March 2020. The organizers announced a new venue: Ramada by Wyndham in Yelahanka, a four star resort in Bangalore.

The 10th edition of Bangalore Open Air was scheduled for 1 April 2023. It was held at Royal Orchid Resort and Convention Centre in Yelahanka, Bangalore.

The Second Edition of the festival took place at Jayamahal Palace on 6 July 2013 and involved bands and artistes from eclectic genres of Heavy Metal. It was headlined by American metal band Iced Earth and Swedish melodic death metal band Dark Tranquillity. The event took place at Jayamahal Palace on 6 July 2013.

The Third Edition of the festival took place on 13 September 2014 and was headlined by Destruction and Rotting Christ. For the first time in the history of Heavy Metal Music the concept of crowd funding was adopted to fund a percentage of the festival. The 4th Edition of the Wacken Open Air Metal Battle, India presented by Bangalore Open Air was held from 19 April to 27 April. The prelims of the competition were held in Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Guwahati & Kolkata.

The 6th and most successful edition of G-Shock Bangalore Open Air was held on 1 July 2017 at Royal Orchid Resorts, Yelahanka, Bangalore( the third consecutive time at the same location.) The lineup consisted of bands from the sub genres of: death metal, thrash metal, and speed metal.

The 7th anniversary edition of G-Shock Bangalore Open Air was held on 7 July 2018 at Aadya Farms and Leisure Resorts, Yelahanka, Bangalore. This edition marked the maiden show of American thrash metal titans Overkill in India along with American death metal band Immolation and French post metal band Alcest, who brought their unique blackgaze sound to India after attempting do so since 2013.

The 8th edition of G-Shock Bangalore Open Air held on 9 February 2019 at Aadya Farms and Leisure Resorts, Yelahanka, Bangalore. Headlining acts include: Black metal giants Abbath and New York Technical death metal outfit Suffocation. On the day of the event the 4 winners of the regional editions of Wacken Metal Battle 2019 from the Indian subcontinent countries: Krur (Nepal), Mass Damnation (Sri Lanka), Trainwreck (Bangladesh), Nephele (India) compete to play for a coveted slot at the Wacken Open Air metal battle in Germany.

The 9th edition of Bangalore Open Air was scheduled for 21 March 2020. The organizers announced a new venue: Ramada by Wyndham in Yelahanka, a four star resort in Bangalore.

The 10th edition of Bangalore Open Air was scheduled for 1 April 2023. It was held at Royal Orchid Resort and Convention Centre in Yelahanka, Bangalore.

Subject: My current ritual with the Chemex
Hi Sarah,
I have been spending an inordinate amount of time thinking about coffee recently. It feels like a strange thing to get obsessed with, but there is something meditative about the process that I have come to rely on heavily during these quiet mornings. I used to just grab a pod for the drip machine while rushing off to work, but lately, I have realized that I was missing out on the entire sensory aspect of the experience. The aroma alone is worth the extra ten minutes it takes to prepare a proper cup. It is less about caffeine and more about creating a small, deliberate routine that anchors my day before I get pulled into the chaos of emails and meetings.
Currently, I am experimenting with a vintage Chemex I found at a local antique shop. The vessel itself is beautiful, with its distinct hourglass shape and the wooden collar secured by a leather tie. Using it changes the way I think about the water and the grounds. I no longer just dump water in; I am paying attention to the temperature, the pour rate, and the bloom. There is a specific moment right after the hot water hits the grounds where they puff up and release carbon dioxide. Watching that cloud rise is oddly satisfying. It reminds me of nature's small processes, even if it is happening on my kitchen counter rather than in a wild forest.
The grind size has been a significant variable in my recent brews. I started too coarse, and the result was a bit watery with noticeable sediment at the bottom of the glass carafe. After a few failed attempts, I found a medium-coarse setting that strikes the perfect balance. The water flows through the filter steadily without any channeling or uneven extraction. This consistency is key because it ensures that every sip tastes the same, from the first pour to the last dregs. I have learned that patience is not just a virtue here but a technical necessity. Rushing the pour leads to bitterness, while stalling too long leads to acidity. It is an endless calibration.
I also switched over to a single-origin bean from a roaster two blocks away. It is an Ethiopian washed variety with notes of blueberry and lemon zest. The flavor profile is incredibly vibrant compared to the muted, chocolatey tones of the commercial brands I used to buy. My palate, it turns out, had been dulled by years of generic coffee. Now, I can taste distinct layers of fruit and nuttiness that I never knew existed. Sharing a cup with my partner has become a weekly ritual where we compare notes and debate which roast date was superior. It adds a genuine layer of connection to our mornings.
Thank you for suggesting I step away from the machine and try something manual. It was exactly what I needed to reset my mornings. I am not sure if I will stick with the Chemex long-term, as the cleanup is a bit tedious, but for now, I am content with the slightly more deliberate approach. I look forward to hearing about any new brew methods or beans you try in your own kitchen. Perhaps we could compare our setups during our next lunch break.
Best,
Alex

Choco tyrannulet

The Choco tyrannulet was originally described as Tyrannulus chrysops albibularis, a subspecies of the golden-faced tyrannulet. Through much of the twentieth century the golden-faced tyrannulet and several other tyrannulets were kept in genus Tyranniscus but a study published in 1977 erected the present genus Zimmerius for them. Following a study published in 2008 that detailed molecular and vocal differences among the golden-faced tyrannulet's subspecies, the Choco tyrannulet was recognized as a full species. The Choco tyrannulet is monotypic.

The Choco tyrannulet is 10.5 to 11.5 cm (4.1 to 4.5 in) long and weighs 6.6 to 8.6 g (0.23 to 0.30 oz). The sexes have the same plumage. Adults have a mottled yellow forehead, dusky lores, a yellow supercilium, a dark stripe through the eye, and golden-brown ear coverts. Their crown, back, and rump are dark olive. Their wings are dusky with yellow edges on the coverts and flight feathers. Their tail is dusky. Their throat is whitish, their breast pale gray with a pale yellow tinge on the sides, their belly whitish, and their vent area pale yellow. They have a gray or brown iris, a small, rounded, black bill, and gray or black legs and feet.

The Choco tyrannulet is a bird of the Chocó bioregion. It is found from southwestern Colombia's Cauca Department south on the western side of the Andes through Ecuador to Santa Elena and Guayas provinces. It inhabits the interior and edges of humid lower montane forest, mature secondary woodland, coffee plantations, and gardens. In elevation it ranges from near sea level to 1,500 m (4,900 ft) in Colombia and to 1,600 m (5,200 ft) in Ecuador.

The Choco tyrannulet feeds on insects and small fruits, especially those of mistletoes (Loranthaceae). It forages singly or in pairs and sometimes joins mixed-species feeding flocks. It feeds mostly in the forest canopy, perching horizontally with its tail cocked and actively moving about and gleaning food while perched or with short flights.

The IUCN has assessed the Choco tyrannulet as being of Least Concern. It has a large range; its population size is not known and is believed to be decreasing. No immediate threats have been identified. It is considered locally common in Colombia and "widespread and often common" in Ecuador. It occurs in several protected areas in Ecuador.

meeting reschedule

Business calendars are rarely static, and the need to adjust schedules is a constant reality for professionals across all industries. When a meeting must be moved, the process is not just about picking a new slot on a digital interface. It is a delicate balance of logistics, respect for others' time, and maintaining a positive professional relationship. Handling a reschedule with care ensures that the disruption is minimal and the working relationship remains strong.

The first step in any effective reschedule is notification. Reach out to all attendees immediately, providing a clear reason for the change without over-explaining. Transparency builds trust, even when the news is inconvenient. Briefly state the new proposed time and date, offering flexibility if the initial suggestion does not work. This proactive approach demonstrates respect for their schedules and reduces the friction of the interaction.

When proposing an alternative time, consider time zones and existing commitments. Use shared calendar tools to find a slot that works for everyone, avoiding the tedious back-and-forth of email chains. If the meeting involves external clients or partners, be especially mindful of their availability. A few extra minutes spent reviewing calendars can save an hour of unproductive coordination later.

Always send a firm confirmation once the new time is agreed upon. Update the original invitation and include any necessary agenda revisions that may stem from the delay. Clarity at this stage prevents misunderstandings and ensures everyone arrives prepared. This final touch reinforces professionalism and shows that you value the group's time.

Ultimately, how you handle a reschedule reflects on your reliability. A calm, organized response turns a potential negative into a neutral administrative task. By prioritizing communication and ease, you maintain momentum in your projects. The next time a conflict arises, remember that a well-executed reschedule preserves both time and goodwill.

Subject: The Changing Rhythm of Ocean Tides
Dear Dr. Martinez,
I hope this message finds you well. I wanted to share a brief overview of observations we have collected on tide patterns near Cape Harbor. Over the past month, our instruments have recorded a consistent shift in the timing of both high and low tides, linked to the recent lunar cycle and atmospheric pressure changes.
Our data indicate that the tide now arrives roughly ten minutes later than the historical average. The amplitude of spring tides has increased by about 12 percent, which could affect shoreline erosion and sediment transport. We have checked the readings against the NOAA tide gauge network, and the discrepancy remains significant.
In addition to the measurements, we have noted subtle changes in intertidal habitats. Certain mussels and barnacles are showing altered settlement patterns, likely responding to longer inundation periods. These ecological shifts may influence the broader food web and merit further monitoring.
I would appreciate any insights you might have regarding the drivers of these variations, especially research on ocean-atmosphere coupling that could explain the observed lag. Please let me know if you would like to discuss the data in more detail or arrange a joint field visit.
Best regards,
Emily Chen
Coastal Oceanographer, Marine Research Institute

The Facilities Department reminds all staff and contractors that the annual parking permit renewal period will begin on Monday, 14 October and close on Friday, 25 October. All current permit holders must complete the online renewal form before the deadline to avoid interruption of parking privileges.

Renewal requests are processed through the campus portal using your employee or contractor ID. After logging in, select "Parking Services," verify your vehicle details, and confirm the renewal fee of $75 for staff or $60 for contractors. Payments can be made by credit card or transferred from your payroll deduction account.

If you change vehicles during the renewal window, update the license-plate information in the system and upload a recent photograph of the new vehicle. Failure to provide accurate data may result in a delayed issuance of the new permit and could require temporary parking in the visitor zones.

Employees who do not renew by the close of business on Friday, 25 October will have their permits deactivated on the following Monday. Deactivated permits will be placed in the unassigned pool and may be reassigned to wait-listed applicants. To reactivate a lapsed permit, you must submit a new application and pay a $20 reinstatement surcharge.

For any questions or technical difficulties, contact the Parking Services Help Desk at ext. 3421 or email parking-support@company.org. We appreciate your cooperation in keeping our parking facilities organized and accessible for everyone.

meeting reschedule

When a meeting needs to be moved, the first step is to communicate the change promptly and clearly. Most professionals rely on a short email or calendar update that states the new date, time, and location, while also confirming the reason for the shift. A concise subject line such as "Rescheduled: Project Kick-off - New Time" helps recipients notice the change among a busy inbox.

Explain the reason without over-detailing. Whether a key participant is unavailable, a venue conflict arises, or a technical issue demands extra preparation, a brief justification shows respect for everyone's schedule. It also reduces the likelihood of follow-up questions that can clutter the thread. Mention any adjusted agenda items so attendees can prepare accordingly.

Provide alternatives when possible. Offering two or three time slots gives participants a chance to select the most convenient option, which can speed up reconfirmation. If the meeting is virtual, include the updated link and any new access codes, and remind participants to check their audio-video setup ahead of time. For in-person gatherings, double-check room bookings and any catering arrangements that may need to be revised.

A polite reminder a day before the new meeting helps solidify attendance. A quick calendar invite with a note that reads "Reminder: Rescheduled meeting tomorrow at 10 a.m." can prevent last-minute confusion. Encourage participants to reply if the new slot still poses a conflict.

Finally, after the meeting has taken place, send a brief follow-up summarizing decisions and next steps. This closes the loop on the reschedule, reinforces accountability, and demonstrates that the change was managed smoothly and professionally.

Subject: Quick tips for your first time with a camera
Hi Jordan,
I heard you are finally ready to pick up a camera again, so I wanted to share a few core concepts that really helped me when I was just starting out. It is easy to get lost in settings, but understanding how light interacts with your sensor is the fundamental key to everything else.
Start by mastering the exposure triangle, which consists of aperture, shutter speed, and ISO. These three elements work together to control how much light reaches your sensor. Aperture dictates depth of field, meaning it controls how much of the image is in focus. A wide aperture blurs the background, while a narrow one keeps more of the scene sharp.
Shutter speed determines how motion is captured in your photo. Fast speeds freeze action, making them perfect for sports or running pets. Slower speeds create motion blur, which can add a sense of energy to waterfalls or city traffic. You need to balance this carefully to avoid blurry images caused by camera shake or moving subjects.
ISO controls the sensitivity of your camera sensor. Keeping it low generally provides cleaner images with less digital noise. However, in low-light situations, you will often need to raise the ISO. The goal is to find the highest setting that still produces acceptable image quality for your specific conditions.
Finally, pay attention to your composition. The rule of thirds is a great starting point, placing your subject along the grid lines rather than dead center. This creates a more dynamic and interesting visual flow. Do not worry about getting it perfect right away, as practice is the only way to build intuition.
Best regards,
Alex

drone regulations

The legal landscape for unmanned aerial vehicles has shifted dramatically over the last decade, transforming recreational flying from a largely unregulated gray area into a highly structured industry. In the United States, the Federal Aviation Administration established Class 107 rules to define how recreational operators can fly drones without a commercial license, but these regulations are far from simple. Many enthusiasts find themselves navigating a complex web of federal, state, and local ordinances that can vary significantly depending on where they live. What is permissible in a rural open field might be strictly prohibited in a nearby suburban neighborhood, creating a patchwork of restrictions that requires constant vigilance from the average flyer.

One of the most critical aspects of compliance involves understanding the controlled airspace surrounding airports and heliports. Drones are generally prohibited from operating in Class B, C, D, and E surface areas without specific authorization from air traffic control. While the LAANC system has streamlined this process by allowing for near real-time approvals through compatible apps, it does not grant blanket permission. Operators must still adhere to specific altitude limits, typically capped at 400 feet above ground level, and must ensure their aircraft has an active Remote ID broadcast capability. This digital license plate is a relatively new requirement aimed at enhancing air traffic safety and helping authorities identify unauthorized or malicious flights quickly.

Local municipal laws often add another layer of complexity that federal guidelines do not address. Cities and counties across the country have enacted their own ordinances regarding noise, privacy, and flight paths, sometimes creating contradictions with broader national standards. For instance, while the FAA sets the baseline for safety in national airspace, a local park authority may ban all aerial operations within its grounds regardless of federal permission. Residents and flyers are therefore advised to check with their city hall or local parks department before taking off, especially in dense urban environments where privacy concerns regarding bystanders and bystander consent have become a significant legal battleground.

The commercial sector faces even more rigorous requirements, demanding a Part 107 certification for the pilot and often a distinct business license for the operation itself. Companies must maintain strict logbooks, file annual announcements, and adhere to visual line of sight rules unless they possess a waiver for beyond visual line of sight operations. Insurance requirements have also become standard industry practice, not just because of liability concerns, but because many clients now require proof of coverage before allowing any drone activity on their private property. This regulatory burden ensures a higher standard of professionalism but creates significant barriers to entry for smaller businesses looking to enter the market.

Enforcement mechanisms for these rules are increasingly sophisticated, leveraging technology to detect and track non-compliant drones. Authorities are empowered to take preemptive measures, including the use of interference systems to disable rogue aircraft or to issue civil penalties that can reach into the tens of thousands of dollars. Ignorance of the law is no longer accepted as a defense, and the burden of proof lies entirely on the operator to demonstrate they were within their permissions. Staying informed through official FAA resources and local government channels is no longer just a best practice but a legal necessity for anyone interested in the skies.

Subject: Quick thoughts on baby sleep routines
Hi Sarah,
I hope this email finds you well. I know we both mentioned feeling overwhelmed by the current sleep situation, so I wanted to share a few strategies that have actually helped our household find some stability recently. It is definitely a journey, but consistency seems to be the key factor in making any progress.
We started by setting a firm bedtime window, aiming for seven to seven thirty PM. This might feel early to you given our adult schedules, but it has worked wonders for us. By starting the wind-down process at this consistent time, we have noticed that our toddler is less likely to overtired, which paradoxically makes it harder for them to settle down later in the evening.
The pre-bed routine is short but sweet. We do bath, book, and lullaby every single night. Keeping the steps identical removes the guesswork for the child. They seem to relax significantly when they know exactly what comes next. It creates a sense of security that helps bridge the gap between activity and rest, making the transition much smoother for everyone involved.
During the nights, we have been trying to wait three full minutes before entering the room. Often, the crying is just a protest blip rather than a genuine distress signal. Giving them that brief window allows them to self-soothe back into sleep. We have had a few sleepless nights during this adjustment period, but the long-term gains in independent sleeping skills have felt very worth the initial struggle.
Please let me know if any of this resonates with your situation. I am happy to swap more tips or just vent if the nights get rough again. We are in this together, and I truly believe we will all get more rest soon enough. Talk soon.
Best,
Alex

Subject: Q3 Budget Planning Framework and Action Items
Hi Team,
I hope you are having a productive week. As we approach the start of the third quarter, it is time to finalize our budget planning process to ensure we remain aligned with our strategic goals. The objective of this quarterly review is not just to look backward, but to proactively manage our resources for the months ahead. We need to establish clear guidelines for spending that reflect both our current financial health and our anticipated growth opportunities. By taking a structured approach now, we can avoid the common pitfall of reactive budgeting, which often leads to overspending in critical areas or underinvestment in high-potential projects. My goal is to gather your input to create a cohesive document that serves as our primary financial guide for the next ninety days.
During our last review, we noticed that our operational costs were running slightly above the initial forecast by a margin of four percent. This variance was primarily driven by unexpected increases in software licensing fees and a slight uptick in utility costs. While these are manageable fluctuations, they highlight the need for greater accuracy in our baseline estimates. For this quarter, I propose that we implement a more conservative approach to variable expenses. This means that any new line items requiring approval will need to demonstrate a clear return on investment or a direct operational necessity. We should also revisit our vendor contracts to see if any renegotiations are possible, particularly with those providers who have not been adequately delivering on their service level agreements.
I would like each of you to review your respective department's current spend and project future needs for Q3. Please identify any areas where you anticipate increased activity, such as hiring, travel, or material procurement, and provide a detailed breakdown of those costs. It is crucial that we distinguish between fixed expenses and discretionary spending in your reports. If there are areas where we can reduce discretionary spending to offset potential increases in fixed costs, please flag them. We have some flexibility in our marketing budget, and shifting resources there might be beneficial if we face constraints in other areas. Your insights on where the money is actually going, rather than just where it is supposed to go, are essential for this process.
We will hold a working session next Tuesday at ten am to discuss these figures in detail. Please bring your preliminary spreadsheets and notes to that meeting so we can dive straight into the data. I want to make sure we align on priorities before we submit the final budget to the board. If you have any immediate concerns or if something urgent comes up that might impact the timeline, please let me know via email before the meeting. I am open to scheduling individual check-ins if you need help refining your numbers or if you want to discuss specific project requirements. My door is always open for these kinds of discussions, and I cannot stress enough the importance of transparency in these estimates.
Thank you for your diligence in preparing these materials. Accurate budget planning is the backbone of our operational stability and long-term success. If we get this right, we set ourselves up for a smoother quarter ahead with fewer surprises. I look forward to reviewing your submissions by end of day Friday so I can consolidate the data beforehand. Let's make sure we are moving in the same direction with a clear understanding of our financial limits and capabilities. I appreciate your cooperation and attention to detail as we wrap up this critical phase of our fiscal year.
Best regards,
Eleanor Vance

raw:
flood preparedness

When heavy rainfalls turn into rising rivers, the threat of flooding can shift from a distant possibility to an immediate emergency. In many communities, a single storm can overwhelm drainage systems, breach levees, or cause flash floods that sweep away everything in their path. Preparing for such events is not just a recommendation; it is a practical necessity that can protect lives, preserve property, and reduce long-term disruption.

The first step in any flood-ready plan is to understand the specific risks that affect your home or workplace. Local government websites often publish floodplain maps, historical water-level data, and alerts about recent weather patterns. By comparing your address to these resources you can gauge whether you live in a high-risk zone, a moderate area, or a low-lying region that is still vulnerable during extreme events. Knowing this baseline helps you allocate resources wisely.

A well-stocked emergency kit can make the difference between comfort and crisis when floodwaters arrive. Include enough bottled water for at least three days, non-perishable food, a manual can-opener, flashlight with extra batteries, a first-aid kit, and a portable radio to receive updates. Personal documents such as identification, insurance policies, and medical records should be sealed in waterproof bags and stored where they can be quickly grabbed. Don't forget a change of clothes and sturdy waterproof shoes.

Protecting the structure of your home before a flood hits can limit damage and speed up recovery. Elevate valuable appliances, electrical panels, and heating systems above the projected flood line whenever possible. Install check valves on sewer lines to prevent backflow, and apply sealants to cracks in foundations, doors, and windows. If you have a basement, consider flood panels or sandbags as temporary barriers, and keep valuable items on higher shelves or in a safe room.

An evacuation plan should be rehearsed regularly so that every family member knows where to go and what to take. Identify multiple routes out of your neighborhood, avoiding low-lying roads that can become impassable. Designate a meeting point outside the flood zone where you can regroup if phone lines fail. Keep a list of emergency contacts, local shelters, and the nearest hospital in a waterproof envelope, and share this information with friends or relatives who may assist you.

After the water recedes, document damage with photos, contact insurers promptly, and follow safety guidelines before re-entering your home.

raw:
lab safety rules

Walking into a laboratory without a clear understanding of safety protocols is akin to stepping onto an active construction site without a hard hat. The environment contains chemicals, biological agents, and equipment that can cause severe injury or death if mishandled. Consequently, every individual who enters the space, whether a seasoned researcher or a new student, must accept that safety is not merely a set of optional guidelines but the fundamental prerequisite for productive work. Ignoring these rules does not just put you at risk; it jeopardizes the safety of your colleagues and the integrity of the entire facility. A proactive mindset where safety is viewed as a personal responsibility rather than a bureaucratic hurdle is the first line of defense against accidents.

Personal protective equipment, often abbreviated as PPE, forms the critical barrier between you and potential hazards. Safety goggles are mandatory whenever there is any chance of chemical splashes, ensuring that your eyes remain protected from corrosive substances. Lab coats made from non-flammable materials serve a dual purpose: they protect your skin from spills and, more importantly, they prevent contaminated clothing from carrying hazardous materials out of the lab into hallways or break rooms. Closed-toe shoes made of leather or heavy synthetic materials are essential to shield your feet from heavy glassware drops or chemical spills. Wearing long pants is equally important, as they provide an extra layer of protection for your legs that shorts or skirts simply cannot offer.

Understanding the specific hazards of the materials you are handling is just as critical as wearing the correct gear. Before beginning any procedure, you must read the Material Safety Data Sheets, which provide detailed information on the toxicity, flammability, and reactivity of each substance. This knowledge allows you to anticipate risks and prepare appropriate emergency measures. For instance, mixing certain cleaning agents can release toxic chlorine gas, a fact that must be known before any cleanup occurs. Always check for compatible storage conditions; some chemicals must be kept in fire-resistant cabinets, while others require refrigeration or specific temperature ranges to remain stable. Knowledge of these interactions prevents dangerous reactions that could lead to explosions or toxic fume release.

Regularly inspecting your equipment and workspace is another pillar of a safe laboratory culture. Before turning on any electrical device, ensure that cords are not frayed and plugs are secure. Glassware must be examined for cracks or chips, as a broken beaker can shatter under pressure or heat, creating sharp shards that pose a significant laceration risk. Spillage should be addressed immediately according to the specific chemical involved; never pour unspecified waste down the drain. If you see a spill that you are not trained to handle, do not attempt to clean it yourself. Instead, evacuate the area if necessary and alert the laboratory supervisor or safety officer immediately to ensure the hazard is neutralized by someone with the proper training and protective equipment.

Finally, knowing how to respond in an emergency is the ultimate safety skill. Every lab member must know the location of fire extinguishers, fire blankets, eyewash stations, and emergency showers. In the event of a chemical splash to the eyes, flushing them with water for at least fifteen minutes is crucial to prevent permanent damage. If a fire breaks out, determine whether it is safe to extinguish it with the appropriate type of extinguisher; otherwise, evacuate the building immediately using the nearest exit. Practice these drills regularly until they become second nature. By embedding these safety practices into your daily routine, you contribute to a culture where accidents are prevented through vigilance, preparation, and respect for the inherent risks of scientific inquiry.

raw:
meeting reschedule

Rescheduling a meeting is one of the most common workplace occurrences, yet it often carries an unspoken weight of anxiety. Many professionals feel a disproportionate sense of guilt when they need to move an appointment, worrying that it reflects poorly on their reliability or disrupts the flow of the team. In reality, however, a single reschedule handled with professionalism is rarely noticed in the grand scheme of a busy workday. The key to maintaining trust is not avoiding the change, but rather how you communicate it and follow up afterward.

Timeliness is the single most important factor when asking to move a meeting. The sooner you provide notice, the more options your counterpart has to adjust their schedule. Waiting until the last minute forces the other person into a difficult position, often requiring them to cancel other commitments or scramble to find a new time slot. By reaching out at least twenty-four hours in advance, you demonstrate respect for their time. This proactive approach minimizes disruption and shows that you value their calendar as much as your own.

When crafting the request, keep your message concise and direct. State clearly that you need to reschedule, provide a brief, honest reason if appropriate, and offer two or three specific new time slots. Avoid lengthy explanations or excessive apologies, which can clutter the message and make the request seem less confident. Offering concrete alternatives takes the burden of finding a new time off their plate, streamlining the process and saving everyone time. Remember that you are not begging for permission; you are coordinating logistics to ensure a successful collaboration.

Once the new time is confirmed, always send a calendar invite as soon as possible. This ensures that both parties have the event locked in, reducing the chance of double-booking or miscommunication. If the meeting involves multiple attendees, send a polite follow-up to the group, apologizing briefly for the inconvenience and expressing excitement to connect at the new time. This closes the loop and reinforces that you are taking ownership of the scheduling mix-up rather than leaving it for others to manage.

Over time, consistent and professional handling of schedule changes builds a reputation for reliability. Even if you frequently need to pivot due to project demands or conflicts, your counterparts will learn to trust that you will communicate clearly and efficiently. Instead of viewing reschedules as breaches of promise, frame them as necessary adjustments in a dynamic work environment. By mastering the art of the polite pivot, you transform a potential moment of friction into a demonstration of effective communication and mutual respect.

From: Fleet Operations Department
To: All Staff
Date: October 12, 2023
Subject: Guidelines for Private Party Vehicle Purchases

The company continues to emphasize strict adherence to cost-control measures when procuring replacement vehicles. While leasing offers predictable costs, buying a high-quality used vehicle from a private seller can yield significant savings over time. Employees approved to purchase used cars for official business use must follow a rigorous vetting process to ensure long-term reliability and minimize unexpected repairs.

Before any negotiation or offer is made, a comprehensive mechanical inspection is mandatory. Do not rely on the seller's verbal assurances or warranty claims. Instead, schedule a pre-purchase inspection with our certified mechanic. This step involves verifying engine health, transmission performance, suspension integrity, and body structural soundness. If the inspection reveals major issues, the transaction should be halted immediately without hesitation.

Price negotiation should be based on industry-standard valuation data. Utilize reputable valuation tools to determine the fair market price for the specific make, model, year, and mileage. Adjust this baseline based on the vehicle's actual condition, as noted in the inspection report. Never pay above the fair market value, and remember that a slightly cheaper car with hidden problems is far more expensive in the long run than a correctly priced, reliable unit.

Document all interactions and offers in writing. Once a price is agreed upon, ensure the bill of sale clearly states the vehicle identification number, odometer reading, and "as is" condition if applicable. Confirm that the title has been properly signed over and that there are no outstanding liens. Delay payment until you have physically verified the vehicle's VIN matches the title document in your hand.

Submit a copy of the signed bill of sale and the mechanic's inspection report to the Fleet Operations Office within forty-eight hours of purchase. Failure to provide these documents will delay the initial fuel card issuance and expense account updates. Proper documentation protects both the employee and the company against future disputes or insurance complications. Please review these steps carefully before proceeding with any vehicle acquisition.

Linhevenator

The type species Linhevenator tani was named and described in 2011 by Xu Xing, Tan Qingwei, Corwin Sullivan, Han Fenglu and Xiao Dong. The generic name combines a reference to the Linhe region with a Latin venator, "hunter". The specific name honours Professor Tan Lin. The holotype of Linhevenator is specimen LHV0021, a partial skeleton of an adult individual, including a cranium and mandible, six dorsal vertebrae, a right scapula, a right humerus, the ilia, a left femur and a left foot. It was found in 2009 and represents the most complete troodontid remains known from the Upper Cretaceous. Its four autapomorphies (unique traits) include a jugal with a lateral flange, a surangular crest that is anteroventrally oriented, the presence of medial expansion near the distal end of the femur, and a wide longitudinal groove present along the distal third of the dorsal surface of the third metatarsal.

Linhevenator is a troodontid, a group of small, bird-like, gracile maniraptorans. All troodontids have many unique features of the skull, such as closely spaced teeth in the lower jaw, and large numbers of teeth. Troodontids have sickle-claws and raptorial hands, and some of the highest non-avian encephalization quotients, meaning they were behaviourally advanced and had keen senses. Linhevenator is a rather large troodontid with an estimated body weight of 23 kg (51 lb), with a length of 1.9 to 2.7 meters (6.2 to 8.9 ft) with an average of 2.2 metres (7.2 feet), based on allometric scaling from Byronosaurus, Stenonychosaurus, and Zanabazar. The arms are relatively short but the humerus is very robust. The describers suggest the arm might have been used for digging or climbing. The first toe was preserved in a lateral position, instead of pointing forwards. Linhevenator has a dromaeosaurid-like pedal digit II, carrying a sickle-claw larger than that of basal troodontids.

Linhevenator was assigned to the Troodontidae by the describers. It possesses a combination of "primitive" (basal) and derived characters, but was found to be a derived troodontid in a phylogenetic analysis, in a polytomy with Troodon and a clade formed by Zanabazar and Saurornithoides. This position was seen by the authors as an indication for an evolutionary trend in the Troodontidae of shortening the forelimbs and for a parallel evolution of large sickle-claws with both the troodontids and the dromaeosaurids.
